title: The AI Era: Better Engineers
summary: As AI transforms software development, are developers becoming better engineers or simply faster coders?

body.content: A few years ago, building a software application meant spending hours writing boilerplate code, debugging syntax errors, searching documentation, and figuring out why something wasn't working.
Today, AI tools can generate entire functions, explain unfamiliar codebases, suggest optimizations, and even help developers build applications from scratch.
1. From Writing Code to Solving Problems
Traditionally, much of a developer's time was spent translating requirements into code. AI is changing that workflow.
When generating code becomes easier, understanding the problem becomes even more valuable.
2. The Hidden Cost of AI-Generated Code
AI-generated code often looks convincing. It may even work perfectly for a simple use case. However, working code and production-ready software are two different things.

items: Two users attempt to update the same record.

body.content: These are engineering problems, not just coding problems. The responsibility for the final implementation still belongs to the engineer.
Knowing the answer and understanding why it works are fundamentally different things. Fundamentals provide the mental models needed to evaluate AI-generated solutions.
4. The Rise of the AI-Augmented Engineer
The future belongs to engineers who can combine technical understanding with effective use of AI tools.
5. What Should Developers Focus on Next?

items: Problem-solving: Break complex problems into smaller pieces.
System design: Understand communication, scalability, and bottlenecks.
Data and databases: Understand storage, indexing, and concurrency.
Critical thinking: Question generated code and validate assumptions.
Adaptability: Learn new tools without abandoning fundamentals.

body.content: Conclusion: Don't Compete With AI at Writing Code
Writing code is becoming easier. Building reliable, scalable, secure, and maintainable systems is still hard.
The goal should be to become an engineer who knows what to build, why to build it, and how to build it well.
